A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NOWA work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections 7–10. The material supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original tamper-localization comparisons, ablations, adversarial evaluations, and physical-camera experiments in Sections 4–5 and the supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports simulation-versus-real null-space residual magnitudes in supplementary Section 10.

M1.justification: The phase-mask design, NSN reconstruction, null-space detector, and joint training losses are unchanged. The revised Preliminaries and NOWA subsections reorganize existing components without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain FFHQ training, COCO evaluation, the same five generative editing methods, noise/compression tests, three adversarial scenarios, and monitor-based physical captures. The new discussion of dust does not document an additional contamination experiment.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MVSS-Net, OSN, PSCC-Net, IML-ViT, HiFi-Net, and EditGuard. Table 2 retains HiFi-Net and EditGuard, and the qualitative comparisons retain the same comparator membership.

E3.justification: Supplementary Section 10 adds the residual norm of the regularized reconstruction's null-space projection as a simulation-versus-real diagnostic. Existing benchmark metrics, splits, training settings, attack sample counts, and capture procedures remain unchanged; no rerun is established.

E4.justification: v3 adds a quantitative diagnostic of residual leakage under real-camera calibration imperfections in supplementary Section 10. The detector-input and phase-mask ablations, degradation tests, and adversarial evaluations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The newly reported approximate residual magnitudes are result estimates, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the three attack F1 scores, 0.901, 0.913, and 0.946, are unchanged. Supplementary Section 10 newly reports residual magnitudes of approximately 10^-5 in simulation and 10^-4 in real captures, described as below tampering-induced residuals.

T1.justification: The optical equations, null-space definition, reconstruction and projection identities, and losses are mathematically unchanged. Numbering the existing null-space definition as Equation 12 adds no theory; the new matched-filter discussion supplies no formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction removes its explicit claim of competitive image-quality preservation measured by PSNR/SSIM, retaining the localization comparison. This is a limited narrowing: the abstract still claims competitive image quality, and the central authentication and security contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Supplementary Section 10 extends the existing calibration caveat with a matched-filter interpretation: structured watermark residuals are distinguished from stochastic optical artifacts despite an elevated real-camera noise floor. The earlier aperture, depth, alignment, and attacker-access limitations remain.

D1.justification: Hardware, fabrication parameters, PSF calibration, optimization settings, fine-tuning, and RAW-image processing instructions are unchanged. No code/data access information is added, and both versions retain the unresolved Nepochs training-duration placeholder.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 72 references and positioning relative to optical watermarking, digital watermarking, and computational photography. Moving established NSN material into Preliminaries does not substantively change its attribution or the novelty claim.

P1.justification: Section 3 is regrouped into Preliminaries, NOWA, and Optimization, with limited explanatory rewriting. v3 also makes grammar corrections, updates the author email, and adds acknowledgments; the overall narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 horizontally reorients the three Attack 3 reconstructed-image examples while retaining their signature maps. The figure/table inventory and table structures remain unchanged, with modest spacing and text-flow adjustments.

improvement.justification: v3 more clearly separates reconstruction background from NOWA and supplements v1's qualitative calibration caveat with explicit residual magnitudes in supplementary Section 10. These changes modestly improve clarity and practical interpretation. The new diagnostic remains brief, without sample counts or uncertainty, and the main benchmark evidence is unchanged.
